newsitem.title: JAPAN: Canada's XCAN sees wheat prices at $3.50 by end-97.
newsitem.headline: Canada's XCAN sees wheat prices at $3.50 by end-97.

text.p: World wheat prices are likely to move in a range between $3.50 and $3.70 a bushel until this summer and stay around $3.50 until the year-end, the head of a Canadian grain trading body said on Friday.
Kenneth Matchett, chief executive officer of XCAN Grain Pool Ltd, said although there had been a bearish trend recently in world wheat prices, he did not believe prices would fall that much.
"I don't think wheat prices will settle back... Until this summer, the prices will be between $3.50 and $3.70," Matchett told Reuters in Tokyo.
Traders said prices have rebounded since last summer on tighter global supplies, but have slipped slightly in recent trade on news of bumper grain production expected in Europe and Australia.
An official of the federation of European Union farmers' groups (COPA) said on Thursday that a further boost in EU wheat production was likely in the 1997 harvest.
Also, Australian Wheat Board officials said on Thursday that Australia is likely to have another larger-than-normal wheat crop in 1997/98 after its record 1996/97 crop.
On Thursday, the March wheat futures on CBOT ended down 3-1/2 at $3.75-3/4 per bushel.
XCAN Grain Pool Ltd is a private grain trading body which is jointly owned by three agricultural cooperatives, one each in the provinces of Alberta, Saskatchewan and Manitoba.
XCAN's Matchett is visiting Japan this week after travelling to South Korea and the Philippines.
